authoredSolutions.61: \(L\) meets \(x-2=-y=z-1\) at \((2+t,-t,1+t)\) and \(2(x+1)=2(y-1)=z+1\) i.e. \(\frac{x+1}{1}=\frac{y-1}{1}=\frac{z+1}{2}\) at \((-1+s,1+s,-1+2s)\), with the joining vector \(\parallel(3,1,2)\). Solving \((s-t-3,s+t+1,2s-t-2)=k(3,1,2)\) gives \(t=-\tfrac43\), so \(L\) passes through \((\tfrac23,\tfrac43,-\tfrac13)\) with direction \((3,1,2)\). Setting \(x=-\tfrac13\) gives \(u=-\tfrac13\Rightarrow(y,z)=(1,-1)\).
authoredSolutions.62: Intersections of \(y^2=4x\) and \(x^2+y^2=5\): \(x^2+4x-5=0\Rightarrow x=1,\ y=\pm2\). Smaller area (right of parabola, inside circle) \(=2\int_0^2\big(\sqrt{5-y^2}-\tfrac{y^2}{4}\big)dy=2\big[1+\tfrac52\sin^{-1}\tfrac{2}{\sqrt5}-\tfrac23\big]=\frac{2}{3}+5\sin^{-1}\!\frac{2}{\sqrt5}\).
authoredSolutions.63: \((2y-5)dy=-3\,dx\Rightarrow y^2-5y=-3x+C\); through \((0,1)\): \(C=-4\), so \((y-\tfrac52)^2=-3(x-\tfrac34)\), a parabola with vertex \((\tfrac34,\tfrac52)\). Then \(2x+3y=\tfrac32+\tfrac{15}{2}=9\).
authoredSolutions.64: Reflect \(P(1,2)\) in the \(x\)-axis to \(P'(1,-2)\); line \(P'R\) (\(R(4,3)\)) meets \(x\)-axis at \(Q=(\tfrac{11}{5},0)\). For parallelogram \(PQRS\), midpoint of \(PR=\) midpoint of \(QS\): \((\tfrac52,\tfrac52)=\big(\tfrac{11/5+h}{2},\tfrac{k}{2}\big)\Rightarrow h=\tfrac{14}{5},\ k=5\). \(hk^2=\tfrac{14}{5}\cdot25=70\).
authoredSolutions.67: Write \(\frac{2\cos x-\sin x}{3\cos x+\sin x}=A(3\cos x+\sin x)+B(\cos x-3\sin x)\Rightarrow A=B=\tfrac12\). Thus \(\int=\tfrac12 x+\tfrac12\log|\sin x+3\cos x|+C\), giving \(\alpha=1,\ \beta=1,\ \gamma=3\), so \(\alpha+\tfrac{\gamma}{\beta}=4\).
authoredSolutions.68: Line \(\tfrac{x}{a}+\tfrac{y}{b}=1\) through \((3,5)\): \(\tfrac3a+\tfrac5b=1\ge2\sqrt{\tfrac{15}{ab}}\Rightarrow ab\ge60\). Minimum area \(=\tfrac12 ab=30\).
authoredSolutions.69: \(\cos\theta\cos(60^\circ-\theta)\cos(60^\circ+\theta)=\tfrac14\cos3\theta\); maximum of \(\cos3\theta\) under the bound is \(\tfrac12\), at \(3\theta\in\{\tfrac{\pi}{3},\tfrac{5\pi}{3},\tfrac{7\pi}{3},\tfrac{11\pi}{3},\tfrac{13\pi}{3},\tfrac{17\pi}{3}\}\), i.e. \(\theta=\tfrac{\pi}{9}(1,5,7,11,13,17)\). Sum \(=\tfrac{\pi}{9}\cdot54=6\pi\).
authoredSolutions.70: \(|\,2\vec a\times3\vec b\,|=6|\vec a\times\vec b|=15\Rightarrow|\vec a\times\vec b|=\tfrac52\). Quadrilateral \(OABC\) area \(=\tfrac12|\overrightarrow{OB}\times\overrightarrow{AC}|\); \(\overrightarrow{OB}=6\vec a+5\vec b,\ \overrightarrow{AC}=3\vec b-2\vec a\), cross \(=28(\vec a\times\vec b)\). Area \(=14\cdot\tfrac52=35\).
authoredSolutions.74: By Cramer + limit: \(x_c=\frac{c+1}{3c+2}\to\tfrac25=h\), \(y_c=\frac{-1}{5(3c+2)}\to-\tfrac1{25}=k\). Circle centre \((\tfrac25,-\tfrac1{25})\) through \((2,0)\): \(25x^2+25y^2-20x+2y-60=0\) (verified: \(100-40-60=0\)).
authoredSolutions.78: Area \(=\tfrac12|\vec a\times\vec b|=5\sqrt6\Rightarrow|\vec a\times\vec b|^2=600\). \(\vec a\times\vec b=(10,\,10-4\alpha,\,3\alpha-20)\Rightarrow25\alpha^2-200\alpha=0\Rightarrow\alpha=8\). \(\vec c=\vec a-\vec b=(3,1,-2)\Rightarrow|\vec c|^2=14\).
authoredSolutions.81: Real roots need \(b^2\ge4ac\) with \(a,b,c\in\{1,2,3,4\}\). Favourable counts: \(b=2{:}1,\ b=3{:}3,\ b=4{:}8\), total \(12\). Probability \(=\tfrac{12}{64}=\tfrac{3}{16}\Rightarrow m+n=19\).
authoredSolutions.83: \(f(x)=1+\lambda^2x-x^3\), local min at \(x=-\tfrac{\lambda}{\sqrt3}\). Numerator of the inequality is always positive, so need \((x+2)(x+3)<0\Rightarrow-3<-\tfrac{\lambda}{\sqrt3}<-2\Rightarrow2\sqrt3<\lambda<3\sqrt3\). \(\alpha^2+\beta^2=12+27=39\).
authoredSolutions.84: Each term \(=\tfrac1n\cdot\frac{1-r^2}{(1+r^2)\sqrt{1+r^4}}\) with \(r=k/n\), so limit \(=\int_0^1\frac{1-r^2}{(1+r^2)\sqrt{1+r^4}}dr\). Sub \(t=r+\tfrac1r\): \(=\tfrac{1}{\sqrt2}\big[\tfrac{\pi}{2}-\sec^{-1}\sqrt2\big]=\tfrac{\pi}{4\sqrt2}=\tfrac{\pi}{\sqrt{32}}\). Thus \(k^2=32\).
authoredSolutions.86: As \(x\to\tfrac\pi2^-\), \(\frac{\tan8x}{\tan7x}\to0\), so left limit \(=(\tfrac87)^0=1=a-8\Rightarrow a=9\). Right limit \((1+|\cot x|)^{b/(a|\tan x|)}\)-type \(=e^{b/a}\) must equal \(1\Rightarrow b=0\). Hence \(a^2+b^2=81\).
authoredSolutions.88: Centre \((h,k)\) equidistant from \((0,0),(1,0)\Rightarrow h=\tfrac12\). Radius \(r=\sqrt{h^2+k^2}=\) distance to origin, and internal tangency to \(x^2+y^2=9\) gives \(r=3-r\Rightarrow r=\tfrac32\). So \(h^2+k^2=r^2=\tfrac94\), and \(4(h^2+k^2)=9\).
authoredSolutions.89: Cauchy on \(\mathbb{N}\) with \(f(1)=1\Rightarrow f(n)=n\). \(\sum_{k=1}^{2022}(\lambda+k)=2022\lambda+\tfrac{2022\cdot2023}{2}\le2022^2\Rightarrow\lambda\le\tfrac{2021}{2}=1010.5\). Largest natural \(\lambda=1010\).
authoredSolutions.152: \(L:(1,2,3)+u(1,1,2)\). Measuring line through \(P=(\tfrac{11}{3},\tfrac{11}{3},\tfrac{19}{3})\) with direction \((2,1,2)\): \(P+s(2,1,2)\). Equating to \(L\) gives \(s=-1,u=\tfrac23\) (consistent). Distance \(=|s|\,|(2,1,2)|=1\cdot 3=3\).
authoredSolutions.153: Differentiating \(\int_0^x\sqrt{1-(y')^2}\,dt=\int_0^x y\,dt\) gives \(\sqrt{1-(y')^2}=y\), so \(1-(y')^2=y^2\), \(y'=\sqrt{1-y^2}\), \(y=\sin x\). Then \(y''=-\sin x\) and \(y''+y+1=-\sin x+\sin x+1=1\).
authoredSolutions.154: \(\mathrm{Re}\frac{z-2i}{z+2i}=0\) means \(z\) subtends a right angle at \(2i,-2i\), so \(z\) lies on the circle of diameter \(2i,-2i\): \(|z|=2\). Max of \(|z-(6+8i)|=|6+8i|+2=10+2=12\).
authoredSolutions.156: Altitude from \(A\perp BC\): \(AP=(-2,2)\perp(\alpha+2,\beta-3)\Rightarrow\beta=\alpha+5\). Altitude from \(B\): \(BP=(3,-2)\perp(\alpha-3,\beta+1)\Rightarrow3\alpha-2\beta-11=0\Rightarrow\alpha=21,\beta=26\). Circumcentre of \(PAB\): \(h=k+2\) and \(6h-4k+11=0\Rightarrow k=-\tfrac{23}{2},h=-\tfrac{19}{2}\). So \((\alpha+\beta)+2(h+k)=47+2(-21)=5\).
authoredSolutions.158: \(\sin3x+\cos3x\in[-\sqrt2,\sqrt2]\), so denominator \(\in[2-\sqrt2,2+\sqrt2]\) and \(f\in[\tfrac{1}{2+\sqrt2},\tfrac{1}{2-\sqrt2}]=[a,b]\). \(ab=\tfrac12,\ a+b=2\), so AM \(\alpha=1\), GM \(\beta=\tfrac{1}{\sqrt2}\), \(\frac{\alpha}{\beta}=\sqrt2\).
authoredSolutions.159: St-I: \(\vec a\times(\vec r-\vec b)=0\Rightarrow\vec r=\vec b+\lambda\vec a\); \(\vec a\cdot\vec r=0\Rightarrow\lambda=-\frac{\vec a\cdot\vec b}{|\vec a|^2}=-\frac{7}{14}=-\tfrac12\), so \(\vec r=(\tfrac32,0,\tfrac12)\), \(|\vec r|=\frac{\sqrt{10}}{2}\neq\sqrt{10}\): incorrect. St-II: \(\cos2A+\cos2B+\cos2C=-1-4\cos A\cos B\cos C\ge-\tfrac32\) (min at equilateral): correct.
authoredSolutions.160: By Leibniz, numerator derivative \(=-3x^2(\sin2x+\cos x)\to0\) at \(x=\tfrac{\pi}{2}\); apply L'Hopital twice. Second derivative \(=-3[2x(\sin2x+\cos x)+x^2(2\cos2x-\sin x)]\to-3\cdot\frac{\pi^2}{4}(-3)=\frac{9\pi^2}{4}\); denominator \(\to2\). Limit \(=\frac{9\pi^2}{8}\).
authoredSolutions.163: \(AB^{-1}=A^{-1}\Rightarrow A^2=B\). \(C=B^{-1}AB\Rightarrow C^2=B^{-1}A^2B=B\), \(C^4=B^2\). Cayley-Hamilton for \(B\): \(B^2-6B+2I=0\) (\(\operatorname{tr}B=6,\det B=2\)). Compare \(C^4+\alpha C^2+\beta I=B^2+\alpha B+\beta I=0\Rightarrow\alpha=-6,\beta=2\). \(2\beta-\alpha=4+6=10\).
authoredSolutions.169: \(\alpha+\beta=\sqrt2,\alpha\beta=-\sqrt3\), so \(P_n=\sqrt2\,P_{n-1}+\sqrt3\,P_{n-2}\). Substituting \(P_{12}=\sqrt2P_{11}+\sqrt3P_{10}\) cancels the \(\sqrt3P_{10}\) and \(\sqrt2P_{11}\) terms, leaving \(-10\sqrt2P_{10}+10P_{11}=10\sqrt3\,P_9\).
authoredSolutions.170: \(\vec a+\vec b=(1,\alpha,2),\ \vec b+\vec c=(-1,\beta,0)\); cross \(=(-2\beta,-2,\alpha+\beta)\). Area \(=\tfrac12\sqrt{4\beta^2+4+(\alpha+\beta)^2}=\tfrac{\sqrt{21}}{2}\Rightarrow4\beta^2+(\alpha+\beta)^2=17\). With \(\alpha\beta=-6\): \((3,-2),(-3,2)\). \(\alpha_1^2+\beta_1^2-\alpha_2\beta_2=13-(-6)=19\).
authoredSolutions.171: Midpoints of chords of \(C\) through \((\alpha,0)\) lie on \(x_0^2+y_0^2=\alpha x_0\); with \(y_0^2=8x_0\): \(x_0(x_0+8-\alpha)=0\). Besides the axis diameter, \(x_0=\alpha-8>0\) gives two more chords when the midpoint is inside \(C\): \(\alpha(\alpha-8)<4\). So \(\alpha\in(8,4+2\sqrt5)=(p,q)\), \((2q-p)^2=(4\sqrt5)^2=80\).
